name: GPU Volume Slicing (Canonical)
definition: A GPU kernel that renders a 2D slice of a 3D volume by mapping screen coordinates to volume coordinates using canonical orientations (Sagittal, Horizontal, Coronal) and applying a translation and scale.
summary: GPU Volume Slicing (Canonical) is a GPU kernel that renders a single 2D slice from a 3D volume using canonical orientations, differing from filters by operating as a direct pixel shader.
